dimension: credential envelopes, key versions, rotation and re-encryption
howToReproduce: Apply the `from` -> `to` replacement in `file`, run `command`, and observe the named case fail. Restore. The three postgres entries run ON THE MAC MINI inside a detached worktree; the laptop's Docker daemon is unreachable by policy and a local run of those three MUST fail to start, which is correct rather than a defect.
notes: TWO mutations SURVIVED their first sweep and both are recorded below with the case that was added to kill them. `cipher-latin1-plaintext` found that this adapter opened three non-ASCII fixtures and had never SEALED one, so the write side's text encoding was untested. `sweep-limit-not-clamped` found a case whose own comment admitted the clamp was "not observable" -- an assertion that could not fail, which is the exact shape this repository has a rule about.

A THIRD DEFECT WAS FOUND BY A TEST RATHER THAN BY A MUTATION, in code this issue wrote: the sweep's first draft asked `needsReEncryption`, which is true only for the `prior` status, so a credential whose root key had been REMOVED from the ring -- `absent`, the fail-closed case -- was counted as `alreadyActive` and the environment was reported complete over a stranded credential. It is now `rootKeyStatus(...) === "active"`, and `sweep-absent-key-counted-as-done` below restores the bug and watches two named cases fail.

No entry is killed by an assertion that compares two things this tranche controls. The six wire-format entries are killed by ciphertexts produced by `internal-packages/tenancy-database/src/secrets.ts`, which this issue does not edit; the three postgres entries are killed by what a real PostgreSQL returns; and the ten sweep entries are killed through `reportRootKeyUsage` and the audit trail -- the store's own record of what happened -- rather than through the sweep's own return value.

mutations.why: SURVIVED the first sweep and is the reason its killing case exists. mutations.killedBy: secrets-key-version.integration.test.ts > a real envelope survives a real PostgreSQL round trip > returns every byte of a format-1 envelope unchanged
mutations.why: A truncating decoder makes every stored envelope permanently unopenable, and NOTHING in the crypto suite — which never touches a database — could tell. This is the join the two halves of the proof meet on.

mutations.command: REAL POSTGRESQL, ON THE MAC MINI: pnpm --filter @platos/adapter-postgres-tenancy exec vitest run secrets-key-version.integration --no-file-parallelism
mutations.killedBy: secrets-key-version.integration.test.ts > returns every byte of a format-1 envelope unchanged
mutations.why: The column-swap this suite exists to catch. Every other secrets suite in the directory fills its envelope with `bytes(32, fill)` — a width, not an envelope — and a swap between two same-width fields would compare equal there.

mutations.command: REAL POSTGRESQL, ON THE MAC MINI: pnpm --filter @platos/adapter-postgres-tenancy exec vitest run secrets-key-version.integration --no-file-parallelism
mutations.killedBy: secrets-key-version.integration.test.ts > stores a 35-byte ciphertext beside a 25-byte one without padding either
mutations.why: `rootKeyVersion` is inside the HKDF info AND the associated data, so a store that defaulted it produces a row nothing can open even though every ciphertext byte survived. Every other suite in the directory writes 1 or 2, so a default of 1 would pass all of them; this one writes NINE.

mutations.killedBy: sweep-root-key-reencryption.test.ts > a credential the sweep cannot move > records a failure, carries on, and refuses to call the sweep complete
mutations.why: THIS MUTATION IS A DEFECT THIS ISSUE WROTE AND THEN FOUND. `domain/key-ring.ts` has THREE statuses and `needsReEncryption` is true for only one of them, so a credential whose key had left the ring was counted as already-done and the environment was reported complete over it. A stranded credential would have been invisible in the one report an operator reads before destroying a key.

mutations.killedBy: sweep-root-key-reencryption.test.ts > the sweep is bounded and resumable > stops at the limit and hands back a cursor
mutations.why: Unbounded is the one thing a job may not be. Without the break, one call rewraps an entire environment in a single invocation and the caller has no way to stop it or to learn how far it got.

mutations.killedBy: sweep-root-key-reencryption.test.ts > clamps a limit above the hard maximum rather than honouring it
mutations.why: SURVIVED the first sweep. The case seeded TWO credentials and asked for a thousand, and its own comment said the clamp was 'not observable in examined' -- an assertion that could not fail. It now seeds SWEEP_HARD_LIMIT + 1, so `examined` is 50 with the clamp and 51 without.

mutations.killedBy: sweep-root-key-reencryption.test.ts > resumes strictly after the cursor and never repeats a credential
mutations.why: An off-by-one on the cursor re-encrypts the boundary credential on every resume: a second envelope at the same revision under the same active key, refused by the store's unique index, and a REWRAP audit row for work that was already done. It is caught by counting REWRAP audits, not by counting the report's own numbers.

mutations.killedBy: sweep-root-key-reencryption.test.ts > stops at the limit and hands back a cursor
mutations.why: A null cursor on an unfinished batch is how a scheduled job restarts from the beginning for ever, re-examining the first fifty credentials on every run and never reaching the rest.

mutations.killedBy: sweep-root-key-reencryption.test.ts > records a failure, carries on, and refuses to call the sweep complete
mutations.why: The whole point of `complete`. A caller that loops until it is true would stop while a credential is still on the old key, and then be told the rotation had finished.

mutations.killedBy: sweep-root-key-reencryption.test.ts > refuses a limit that is not a positive integer
mutations.why: A limit of zero is a sweep that examines nothing and reports `complete: false` for ever; a fractional one makes `examined >= limit` fire in the middle of a credential. Both are refused with the same code `purge-retired-versions.ts` refuses them with.

mutations.killedBy: sweep-root-key-reencryption.test.ts > reports the failure's CODE and never its reason or its envelope
mutations.why: `domain/errors.ts` collapses nine reasons into one code precisely so a caller cannot tell a missing credential from a tampered envelope from a retired root key. A report that widened the skip by one field would re-open that oracle for every credential a sweep touched.

mutations.killedBy: sweep-root-key-reencryption.test.ts > who may run a sweep > refuses a read-only operator grant
mutations.why: Metadata access is what `describeCredential` needs; a sweep WRITES an envelope for every credential in the environment. Widening it would let a read-only console session rewrap a tenant's whole vault.
